entities.name: Gaius Licinius Macer
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Licinius Macer was a prominent Roman annalist and politician of the late Republic period.

Born into a prominent family in Rome, Macer rose to prominence through his writings on Roman history and politics.

As a key figure associated with the Second Triumvirate, Macer played a significant role in shaping the Republican agenda in the 1st century BCE.

His annals, which chronicled the events of the late Republic, provided valuable insights into the political machinations of the time.

Macer's legacy extends beyond his own writings, as he helped shape the intellectual landscape of ancient Rome and paved the way for future generations of historians and politicians.
